sample_unit: benchmark evaluations of 5 models at 3 precision levels

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety change after quantization and recovery fine-tuning across tasks
links.effect: INT8 max degradation -1.9% to 1.9%; INT4 degradation substantial and model-dependent (BioMistral-7B -19.7% on MedMCQA). Recovery methods raised MedMCQA but further degraded MedQA.
links.quote: We additionally test two recovery methods, clinical calibration substitution and QLoRA fine-tuning, both producing the same trade-off: MedMCQA recovers while MedQA further degrades, indicating recovery strategies require task-specific validation rather than being assumed universally beneficial.

links.outcome: Performance on HealthBench emergency-risk subgroup under INT4 quantization
links.effect: Qwen2.5-7B degrades by 26.8% on the emergency-risk subgroup under INT4; results are model-dependent, and INT8 is broadly safe.
links.quote: On HealthBench's emergency-risk subgroup, Qwen2.5-7B degrades by 26.8% under INT4, suggesting high-risk scenarios are disproportionately vulnerable to compression.

unlisted_practices: Validating model quantization level (INT8 vs INT4) per model and per task before edge deployment
Assessing safety refusal robustness separately from accuracy after model compression

screen.practice: quantization precision selection with task-specific validation
screen.reason: Empirically tests the safety and accuracy impact of model quantization (GPTQ-INT8/INT4) and recovery techniques across multiple clinical benchmarks.
